where_it_appears: Browser tab, bookmark bar, history list
what_fails_first: Counters fill in and become solid dots. Any wordmark becomes a grey smear; this slot is mark-only

where_it_appears: Retina tab, Windows taskbar, some search results
what_fails_first: Thin strokes drop to one pixel and alias into grey. Two-tone marks lose the lighter tone

where_it_appears: Windows site shortcut, some Android contexts
what_fails_first: Fine detail survives but a wordmark of more than about five characters is still unreadable

where_it_appears: iOS home screen. Corners are masked by the OS; do not pre-round
what_fails_first: Nothing structural. The usual failure is a designer pre-applying rounded corners, which the OS then rounds again

where_it_appears: Android home screen, PWA install prompt
what_fails_first: Anything outside the centre circle of radius 40% of width may be cropped by the platform mask

where_it_appears: Splash screen, store listing, PWA maskable master
what_fails_first: Nothing at this size. This is the master; derive the smaller slots from it rather than upscaling

where_it_appears: Profile photo on most platforms, usually displayed as a circle
what_fails_first: Square-composed marks lose their corners to the circular crop. Compose to the inscribed circle
